welcome.title: Welcome to CamTrap Verify
welcome.subtitle: This tool lets you verify the presence of a species at specific locations and time periods, confirming or discarding the automatic detections. When you're done, you'll get a CamtrapDP with the confirmed observations marked as human-reviewed, along with naive vs. verified detection histories ready for occupancy models.

gallery.title: Detection verification
gallery.intro_hint: The detection events shown below are separated by {{gap}} seconds, captured at different locations and time occasions of {{days}} days, corresponding to observations with a detection confidence of {{minScore}} or higher. For each one, confirm whether the detection event contains one or more individuals of the species {{species}}. If you confirm the species' presence in a detection event, its presence will be considered verified for that location during the corresponding time occasion, and no further detection events from that same occasion will need to be reviewed. If you cannot confirm its presence, a new detection event captured at the same location and during the same time occasion will be shown to continue the verification.

help.title: Help — CamTrap Verify
help.what_body: A tool for iteratively reviewing and validating species detections from camera traps. It takes a CamtrapDP directory as input and produces a new CamtrapDP with the verification status of each record.
workflow_steps: Configure the CamtrapDP directory, target species, study period and sampling parameters.
For each species, review sampling occasions one by one.
Each occasion shows the detection event with the highest detection confidence. Confirm or reject it.
When you save, if any occasions remain unconfirmed, a second round opens with the next detection event for each occasion.
Once all species are complete, go to Results to export the verified CamtrapDP.

concepts.def: A time window of N days per location. All images from the same site within that window form one occasion.
A group of images taken at the same location less than N seconds apart (configured under 'Gap between detection events').
Each round shows the highest-confidence unreviewed detection event for each occasion. If rejected in round 1, the next lower-confidence detection event appears in round 2.
The maximum classification probability across all images in a detection event, as assigned by the AI model.

help.decisions_body: Confirming means the species is present in that occasion and location. Rejecting means the detection is incorrect. An occasion closes as soon as one detection event is confirmed.

results.title: Verification results
results.subtitle: Each row is an event — unique combination of site × occasion × species.
results.datapackage_generated: The exported package's datapackage.json was auto-generated because the source had none. The following fields are placeholders, not derived from your data — edit them before treating this as a citable/archival package:
results.output_hint: The session folder contains two subdirectories: camtrap_dp_verified/ with the original CamtrapDP modified — confirmed observations have classificationMethod='human', classificationProbability=1.0 and classifiedBy='expert_review'; and occupancy_inputs/ with per-species naive and verified detection histories (dethist_naive_*.csv, dethist_verified_*.csv) plus cell_status_*.csv, giving the status of each cell (1, 0, pending, unreviewed or inactive), a camera operation matrix, a verification summary and a review effort report.
results.occupancy_hint: Comparison of occupancy (ψ) and detection (p) probabilities estimated from the unreviewed detections versus the manually verified ones. Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.
results.pending_title: {{n}} occasions are still pending expert review
results.pending_hint: They appear as NA in dethist_verified_*.csv, just like occasions with an inactive camera. To tell them apart, see cell_status_*.csv (values pending and inactive). You can export the session from the species index so that someone else reviews them.

mc.title: Classifiers and reference
mc.desc: Each classifier is a CamtrapDP folder of the same photos: one or more AI classifiers (e.g. DeepFaune, a YOLO model) and, optionally, a human reference (e.g. the Zooniverse volunteers' labels). The app recalculates one probability per photo and species, uses the reference to choose how to calculate it, and removes the detection events not worth reviewing. The result is a new CamtrapDP that the session then uses.
mc.classifiers_desc: One row per classifier. AI classifiers propose the detections: you can use one or several. The reference (optional) is the labels given by people, taken as truth: it measures the AI classifiers, teaches the app how much to trust each one, chooses the method and decides which events can be removed. Leave its row empty if you have no reference.
mc.name: Name
mc.reference_hint: Photos are matched by mediaID: every folder must use the same IDs.
mc.period_hint: {{n}} photos in the AI classifiers' folders. The session will use this same period, occasion length and gap.
mc.species_desc: Tick the target species: these are the species reviewed afterwards. Species of the same group (e.g. red and fallow deer in Cervidae) are scored together and then split animal by animal. Leave the group empty for a species on its own, pick a proposed one or type any name.
mc.label: Label
mc.no_reference: Without a reference the probabilities are combined by agreement between classifiers and no events are removed.
mc.filter_cells_hint: Recommended when the result is a detection history (presence per site and occasion). Per species, removes the events below the highest threshold that still keeps a true event in the chosen share of the cells where the reference confirms the species. It keeps presence, not every event: on Doñana 2023 it removed 26 % of the events and kept every cell, and 83 % of the true events.
mc.filter_events_hint: The threshold keeps the chosen share of the reference's true events instead of cells. It removes fewer events; use it if the verified events will be used for counts or detection rates.
mc.filter_none_hint: Nothing is removed: the new probability only changes the order in which the events are shown.
mc.use_reference: Photos reviewed by the reference: use its verdict (confirmed go up, rejected go down)
mc.running: Running: this can take a few minutes on large archives.
mc.opening: Opening the dataset… (it is read again: this can take a minute)
mc.name_hint: Type a short name for each classifier (e.g. DeepFaune, YOLO, Zooniverse). It identifies the classifier in the tables and in the diagnostics, so each one needs a different name.
mc.name_duplicate: Two classifiers are called "{{name}}". Give each one a different name.
mc.read_labels_required: Required: the app reads which labels and dates each classifier has. The period, the species and the options appear after this step.
mc.labels_read: Labels read: {{n}} photos. If you change a classifier, read them again.
mc.missing_ai: Add at least one AI classifier.
mc.missing_rows: Fill in a name and a folder for each classifier.
mc.missing_species: Tick at least one target species.
mc.missing_period: Check the study period: the start must be before the end.
mc.single_ai_no_reference: With one AI classifier and no reference nothing changes: the probabilities stay those of the classifier and no event is removed. Add a reference, or open the classifier's CamtrapDP directly (CamtrapDP directory).
mc.remote_paths_info: {{pct}} % of the photos in the AI classifiers' media.csv are web addresses (e.g. Trapper) instead of paths on this computer. That is fine: in the Images directory step, choose the folder that holds the photos, and the app finds each one by its camera folder (deploymentID) and its file name, also inside subfolders (e.g. R0025\r0025-dona_0011) and with another extension (.JPEG or .jpg).
mc.output_title: Where to save the combined dataset
mc.output_hint: A new folder is created inside {{dir}} with the CamtrapDP and, in its multiclassifier subfolder, the diagnostics. Leave the name empty to use multiclassifier_ and the date and time. An existing folder that already holds files is never overwritten.
mc.groups_how: How groups are proposed: species are put together when some classifier uses their genus (e.g. Martes) or their family (e.g. Cervidae) as a label. Mammal families come from the Mammal Diversity Database (all 1,363 mammal genera), so this also works outside Europe. For other taxa, such as birds, type the group yourself. The groups you use are remembered and proposed again the next time you choose those species.
mc.other_labels_title: Labels that are not a species
mc.other_labels_desc: These labels (e.g. Cervidae, Leporidae, Aves) can't be ticked as target species, because the review is per species and they don't say which one. They are not lost: a label that is a group's name means "an animal of that group, species unknown", which counts for the group's presence while the species is decided animal by animal from the other classifiers. Any other label (e.g. a genus or a common name such as deer) can be told to mean a group or a species; otherwise it counts as another animal.
mc.label_group_auto: Group label: an animal of {{species}}, species unknown
mc.how_title: How the new probability is calculated
mc.how_intro: Every photo gets a new probability for each target species. The review uses it to show the most likely detection events first and to leave out those not worth reviewing. It is the product of two parts:
mc.how_presence: Is there an animal of the species' group in the photo? Each AI classifier that saw the photo says something about it: the group or one of its species with a probability, empty, another animal, a person, or nothing because it didn't process that photo. The method (below) decides how much each of these counts.
mc.how_species: Only for groups with several species (e.g. red and fallow deer). Boxes of different classifiers that overlap are taken as the same animal, each animal gets a probability for each species from the classifiers' votes, and the photo takes, for each species, the animal where that species is clearest. So a photo with a red deer and a fallow deer can be high for both, and a lone fallow deer seen by one classifier stays low.
mc.how_example: Example from Doñana 2023 (photo 5017409): YOLO says horse with 0.93, DeepFaune says empty and no neighbouring photo has horses. Highest probability gives 0.93; agreement levels give (0 + 0.93) / 2 = 0.47, below any photo where both agree; learned from the reference, 0.53; with neighbouring photos, 0.32. With 14 neighbouring photos of horses it would be 0.68.
mc.how_methods: Each adds one idea to the one before:
mc.how_m_raw: the highest probability that any classifier gave (what a simple merge does). Only a baseline: it is never chosen.
mc.how_m_levels: first how many classifiers agree, then the probability: a photo where two agree is always above one where only one does. Needs no reference.
mc.how_m_levels_calibrated: as agreement levels, but each classifier's probability is first turned into the precision it really has for that group, measured against the reference, so 0.9 means the same for every classifier.
mc.how_m_learned: a logistic regression learns from the reference how much each situation weighs: "YOLO says the group with probability p", "DeepFaune says empty", "says another animal", "didn't see the photo", and so on.
mc.how_m_learned_context: as learned, plus the neighbouring photos of the same camera (±20 s): how many were given the same group or another one and, for the species, which species the neighbours and the camera usually have.
mc.how_choice: Only with a reference. Each method scores every photo with a model trained without that photo's camera (the cameras are split into 5 blocks), so it can't learn the answer. Then the reviewer's work is counted: in cells where the reference confirms the species, the events shown before the first true one; in the other cells, every event left after the filter, since each has to be rejected. The method with the least work wins, as long as it keeps a true event in the share of cells set in the advanced options (99 %). The sites are resampled 300 times: methods whose difference with the best is not clear are tied, and the tie is broken as set in the advanced options.
mc.how_filter: For each species, the threshold is the highest score that still leaves a true event in 99 % of the cells (site × occasion) where the reference confirms the species: in each of those cells the best of its true events is looked at, and the threshold leaves 99 % of them above it. It is applied to every event: an event below it is removed unless it is the best of its cell, the reference confirmed it, or the reference marked an animal it couldn't identify. Species with fewer than 100 cells confirmed by the reference are not filtered, because a 1 % loss can't be estimated with so few.
mc.how_reference: On the photos the reference reviewed, its verdict replaces the model's: confirmed → presence 1 (top of the list, never removed); another animal or a person → ×0.05; empty → ×0.10 (lowered, not deleted).
mc.how_noref: Without a reference, agreement levels are used and nothing is removed: only the order of the events changes.
mc.how_more: The full explanation, with the results on the Doñana 2023 archive, is in the documentation:
mc.how_more_link: Combining several classifiers: methods and workflow
mc.retention_hint: The 99 % of the filter. A lower value removes more events and accepts losing more: at 95 %, about 1 cell in 20 where the species is present may keep no true event to review, and could end up as not detected.
mc.tie_ambiguous_hint: Among the tied methods, the one with the lowest mean probability of the second species in photos of groups with several species: the one that most often says clearly which species each photo is.
mc.tie_simple_hint: Among the tied methods, the first of the list: the one with fewest assumptions, safer if the reference photos are not like the rest.
mc.tie_none_hint: The method with fewest events to look at, even when the difference is not significant.
mc.use_reference_hint: Recommended: it uses what people already checked. Confirmed photos go to the top and are never removed; photos the reference rejected are lowered (×0.05 for another animal or a person, ×0.10 for empty), not deleted.
mc.always_kept: Always kept, whatever the options: the best event of each cell, the events the reference confirmed and those with an animal it couldn't identify.
mc.sum_method: Method chosen: {{name}}. Among the methods that keep a true event in {{share}} of the cells with the species, it leaves the fewest events to look at ({{rounds}}).
mc.sum_rule_ambiguous: the tie was broken by the clearest species (mean probability of the second species: {{value}}).
mc.sum_rule_simple: the simplest of them was taken.
mc.sum_rule_none: the one with fewest events was taken.
mc.sum_method_noref: Without a reference the probabilities were combined with {{name}} and nothing was removed.
mc.sum_reorder: Nothing was removed: only the order of the events changed.
mc.sum_cells_all: Every cell with the species keeps at least one event.
mc.sum_species_nofilter: not filtered: only {{n}} cells confirmed by the reference, at least {{min}} are needed.
mc.sum_two: Photos with two species of the same group at 0.5 or more: {{before}} → {{after}}.
mc.sum_check: To see what was removed before reviewing, open multiclassifier/events_with_score.csv in the new folder: each event with its new score, its previous score and whether it was kept.
mc.sum_method_tie_one: {{others}} left a number that is not clearly different (the 95 % interval of the difference includes 0), so
mc.sum_method_tie_other: {{others}} left numbers that are not clearly different (the 95 % interval of the difference includes 0), so
